entities.summary:
The Fortaleza de Santa Teresa, or Fortaleza Santa Tereza is a military fortification located 36 km (22 mi) south of Chuy and 305 km (190 mi) northeast of Montevideo on Route 9, in the Rocha Department of eastern Uruguay. It lies about 800 m (2,600 ft) from the coast at Playa la Moza, almost halfway between Angostura and La Coronilla ,
north of Punta del Diablo and roughly 4 km (2.5 mi) northeast of the northeast bank of the Laguna Negra. It lies within the Santa Teresa National Park. It was erected from October 1762 by the Portuguese, having abandoned the attempt at building a fort in Maldonado and leaving the Fuerte San Miguel.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Fortaleza de Santa Teresa played a crucial role in the Portuguese colonization of Uruguay, serving as a strategic military outpost and facilitating the expansion of European influence in the region. Its construction in 1762 marked a significant milestone in the history of South American exploration.
